G0.text: People on foot are not harmed by the KAUHA-equipped loader operating autonomously within its scope, given assumptions A1–A3.

C0.text: KAUHA retrofit kit on a 15.5 t articulated wheel loader, loading 20 t trucks from stockpiles on a fenced aggregates yard, with a remote supervisor. Evidence is from the digital twin, the multi-process SIL and formal proofs.

A1.text: People on foot are kept out of the dig and dock zones by access control (barriers, tags or light curtains at the zone entries). The truck driver stays in the cab, or the cab-door switch reports otherwise (SR-14).

A2.text: The safety scanners, speed sensors, e-stops and relays are certified parts wired two-channel and report the truth within their stated response times.

A3.text: The braking budget (reaction 0.47 s, 2.5 m/s² dry, 1.5 m/s² winter) holds on the target machine. To be measured before field trials.

S0.text: Argue over each identified hazard (docs/safety/hazards.yaml), then over the work that only hardware and certification can close.

H1.text: H1: Person struck by the machine travelling forward is controlled.

H1.S.text: Argue that each allocated safety requirement is correctly implemented, then validate the integrated system against the hazard.

H1.S.SR-02.text: SR-02 is correctly implemented: An object in the protective field of the active direction (or the side fields while moving) shall cause a protective stop within one PLC cycle of the scanner output. Each field shall cover the swept path over the stopping distance at the top speed of its band, for every articulation angle in its sector.

evidence.text: A violated front protective field of the selected set stops the machine in the same cycle, unless the front field is in supervised teleop recovery.
Same for the rear protective field (reversing, or at standstill).
Same for the side fields while the machine moves.
A scanner fault stops the machine.

H1.S.SR-03.text: SR-03 is correctly implemented: An object in the warning field shall limit speed to 1.0 m/s without stopping. The limit holds for 2 s after the field clears. Warning fields are not evaluated inside the access-controlled dig and dock zones, where they would only ever see the stockpile or the truck.

evidence.text: While the warning hold is active the speed limit is at most the warning speed.

H1.S.SR-04.text: SR-04 is correctly implemented: Speed shall be monitored against the active limit. After a limit drops, the speed shall follow a 0.8 m/s² ramp, starting after a 0.3 s reaction time. The autonomous speed limit shall not exceed the speed the protective field range can protect for the current braking budget (dry or winter), less the overspeed tolerance. While the brakes are released on a travel field set, the measured speed shall never exceed the speed that set's protective field can stop from.

evidence.text: The commanded speed limit never exceeds the speed the scanners can protect.
Whenever the brakes are released on a travel field set, the measured speed is within what that set's protective field can stop from.

H1.S.SR-08.text: SR-08 is correctly implemented: Disagreement between the two speed channels of more than 0.3 m/s for more than 0.2 s shall cause a stop.

evidence.text: The two speed channels disagreeing by more than 0.3 m/s for more than 0.2 s stops the machine.

H1.V.text: Integrated validation shows person struck by the machine travelling forward does not occur.

H1.V.shift.text: 18 simulated 60-min shifts (6 configurations): 0 contacts with the moving machine, 0 protective-field entries while moving, 0.0 s under a raised bucket; closest approach 0.73 m

H1.V.adv.text: Adversarial search (rules-kept): 80 episodes, CMA-ES vs random; 0 contacts; worst clearance found 0.07 m (random search: 0.23 m)

H1.V.adv-carry.text: Adversarial search (load-and-carry site, rules-kept): 58 episodes, CMA-ES vs random; 0 contacts; worst clearance found 0.09 m (random search: 0.09 m)

H3.text: H3: Person beside the frames crushed at the articulation or brushed by the bucket is controlled.

H3.S.text: Argue that each allocated safety requirement is correctly implemented, then validate the integrated system against the hazard.

H3.S.SR-02.text: SR-02 is correctly implemented: An object in the protective field of the active direction (or the side fields while moving) shall cause a protective stop within one PLC cycle of the scanner output. Each field shall cover the swept path over the stopping distance at the top speed of its band, for every articulation angle in its sector.

evidence.text: A violated front protective field of the selected set stops the machine in the same cycle, unless the front field is in supervised teleop recovery.
Same for the rear protective field (reversing, or at standstill).
Same for the side fields while the machine moves.
A scanner fault stops the machine.

H3.S.SR-12.text: SR-12 is correctly implemented: In TELEOP, a supervisor reset with an occupied protective field shall enter recovery, adding that field to any already in recovery. The speed limit is 0.5 m/s (0.3 m/s for the side fields) from the first recovery cycle, motion toward the occupied field trips again, and boom/bucket motion is disabled until the field clears. Recovery from a side-field stop is refused, and recovery motion stops, while the 0.35 m contact band beside either frame is occupied: beside the frame no direction of travel moves away from a person, because the bucket is wider than the front frame. Inside the access-controlled dig zone, and the dock zone while the truck's cab door is closed, the band does not block recovery (the object there is the pile flank or the truck).

evidence.text: The implement (boom, bucket) is never enabled during recovery.
During recovery from a front stop, moving forward stops the machine; from a rear stop, reversing stops it.
During recovery from a side stop, an occupied contact band stops the machine (outside the access-controlled zones).
Recovery exists only in TELEOP.
While recovering with the brakes released, the speed limit is creep speed (0.5 m/s, 0.3 m/s for a side stop).

H3.V.text: Integrated validation shows person beside the frames crushed at the articulation or brushed by the bucket does not occur.

H5.S.SR-14.text: SR-14 is correctly implemented: While the cab door of the truck in the bay is open, the dock field set shall not be granted; if the door opens while docking, the machine shall make a protective stop that clears 3 s after the door closes.

evidence.text: The dock field set is never active while the truck's cab door is open.
The cab door opening while docking in the dock zone stops the machine.

H5.S.SR-16.text: SR-16 is correctly implemented: Outside the dig zone, a person between the front tyres and the bucket (2.0–2.8 m ahead of the front axle, any boom position; 2.8–3.35 m, any boom position, not beside a docked truck), under the raised bucket (2.8–5.1 m, bucket bottom above 1.0 m; not beside a docked truck), or beside the front frame while reversing (not beside a docked truck) shall cause a protective stop that holds the boom. Teleop recovery may only back away.

evidence.text: Outside the dig zone, anyone between the front tyres and the bucket (near field at any boom position; mid field at any boom position, except beside a docked truck) or under the raised bucket (far field, except beside a docked truck) stops travel and holds the boom, unless backing away in recovery.
While reversing, anyone beside the front frame stops the machine (outside the dig zone and a docked truck), unless backing away from a side stop in recovery.
During recovery from an under-bucket stop, moving forward stops the machine, and the boom stays held.

H5.V.text: Integrated validation shows person between the truck and the loader, or under the raised bucket does not occur.
